clue.text: Decide bone is broken in mutiny

indicators.note: something broken is smashed into pieces, so the letters of the words before it are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to snap a bone as an act of rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' looks like the verb of the surface but is part of the fodder; 'broken' alone signals the shuffle of all three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutiny is open refusal to obey orders, a form of rebellion against authority.

clue.text: Start to grieve in awful lament

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: awful means dire, dreadful

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only the first letter of grieve is used

parts.note: its first letter is G

explanation.surface: Someone begins mourning with a dreadful wail.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a mournful song or hymn sung for the dead, a musical expression of grief.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who watches an event
second meaning: The ..., a long-running British weekly political magazine

explanation.walkthrough: The Observer is also a British Sunday newspaper, which makes the clue look like a pair of publications; only the second word names one.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator is a person watching a game or show, and The Spectator is a British weekly current-affairs title.

indicators.note: around says the first word wraps itself about the second

parts.note: to carry is to bear, so carries gives bears
G is the abbreviation for good, so two of them give goods

explanation.surface: A porter hauls merchandise on behalf of the very poor.
explanation.definitionFit: Beggars are people so poor they ask for alms, the same destitute class as paupers.

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, so the first word holds the second within it

parts.note: informally, gasping means very thirsty, so dry
sinful means evil

explanation.surface: Someone panting in a passionate clinch with wicked depravity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gasping' is the British informal sense 'desperate for a drink', hence DRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Devilry is wicked, mischievous behaviour, the sort of corruption that depravity also names.

parts.note: read literally, the body parts that do the listening, rather than imagining sounds

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing things' usually means imagining noises that aren't there; read literally it is the organs that do the hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ears are the body's organs of hearing, the parts that literally do the listening.

clue.text: Belief includes detailed location for peak

indicators.note: includes says the first word takes the second inside it

parts.note: a credo is a statement of belief

indicators.note: de-tailed: the word has its tail, its final letter, cut off

parts.note: a scene is the location where something happens

explanation.surface: A creed spells out exactly where the summit is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' looks like 'thorough' but is read as de-tailed, a word with its tail cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: A crescendo is the climax or highest point of something building up, so a peak.

parts.note: food that has gone bad is off
the tip of something is its end

explanation.surface: A blunt-ended sewing needle is no use.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to irritate or provoke them, much as to offend is to upset them.

parts.note: one is I in Roman numerals, so one's is I'S
to sue is to take legal action against, so prosecuted gives sued

explanation.surface: A defendant is tried in court and then set free.
explanation.definitionFit: When a statement or product is issued it is published or put out, i.e. released.

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to have them inside, so the first word holds the second

parts.note: one's face is one's appearance
R, for Regina, is the abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A comic routine of pratfalls is put on to amuse the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Farce is broad comedy built on improbable situations and physical humour such as pratfalls.

clue.text: End of testing finished head teacher

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: its last letter is G
something finished is over
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: With exams over, the head teacher can relax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head teacher' looks like one phrase; 'head' is NESS, a headland, and 'teacher' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A governess is a woman employed to teach children in a private household.

clue.text: United in level score at last

parts.note: level means even

indicators.note: in says the letter goes inside the other words

parts.note: a score is a tally
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names

explanation.surface: A football report: Manchester United finally pull the score level.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventually means in the end, after delay, which is what finally or at last says.

indicators.note: Partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some raw, unbleached fabric is only partly white.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecru is unbleached linen or a fabric of that greyish-beige colour, so a kind of cloth.

indicators.note: to arrest someone is to hold them, so the first word holds the second inside

parts.note: demos are protest rallies

indicators.note: dis-heartened: the word loses its heart, its middle letter

explanation.surface: Protest marches in which despondent people are detained bring them low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' looks like a mood but is read as dis-heartened: a word losing its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: To demote someone is to reduce their rank, which is to degrade them in status.

parts.note: minute means very small, little
a boy is a male who grows into a man, so the word is loosely man

explanation.surface: Little Boy, the atomic bomb dropped on Hiroshima, is set beside a second armament.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Boy was the atomic bomb dropped on Hiroshima, which is why 'another weapon' fits; the two words of its name then split apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Minuteman is an American intercontinental ballistic missile, a nuclear weapon like the Little Boy bomb.

clue.text: Following yen, deserved to be desired

indicators.note: following says the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen
to have earned something is to have deserved it

explanation.surface: After some cash, a reward felt deserved and wished for.
explanation.definitionFit: To have yearned for something is to have longed for it, wanted it intensely.

clue.text: Second crop scattered at the farm

indicators.note: things scattered are thrown about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A further harvest is sown broadly about the farm.
explanation.walkthrough: The word now usually means consequences, but its original sense is a second mowing of grass in a season.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally an after-mowing, aftermath is a second growth of grass cut later in the season.

indicators.note: in says one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a parade is a march
an actor on stage is on

explanation.surface: Performing in a procession organised for the king.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch is a sovereign ruler, and a king is one example, hence the question mark.

indicators.note: taking means taking in, so the first word holds the letter inside

parts.note: Inspector Morse is the Oxford detective of Colin Dexter's novels and the TV series
O is the abbreviation for an over in cricket

explanation.surface: A sulky detective takes charge of a case.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Morse was famously gloomy, which suits the surface; an over is a set of six balls in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Morose means sullen and gloomy, ill-tempered in the way a moody person is.

clue.text: Renegade jerk after the woman's sweetheart

indicators.note: after says this piece comes behind the others

parts.note: her means belonging to the woman
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter, E
a tic is an involuntary jerk

explanation.surface: A traitor twitches as he chases a girl's lover.
explanation.definitionFit: A heretic departs from accepted doctrine, a dissenter or defector like a renegade.

clue.text: Proposals backing technology to stop satellites

indicators.note: to stop means to plug, so the reversed letters go inside

parts.note: moons are natural satellites of planets

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: IT is short for information technology

explanation.surface: Plans to halt satellites using reverse technology.
explanation.definitionFit: Motions are formal proposals put to a meeting or assembly for debate and a vote.

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters are spread across these words

explanation.surface: Players in a match took home a trophy.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento is a keepsake or souvenir, and a trophy is a token kept as such a reminder.

parts.note: Sol is the Latin name for the sun
an ace is a star performer

explanation.surface: Two heavenly bodies offer comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: Solace is comfort in distress, and to cheer someone is to comfort them in a sad time.

clue.text: Ceremony is just for the audience

indicators.note: an audience listens, so the word is as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: just means right, fair

explanation.surface: A ritual performed only for spectators.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite is a formal religious or ceremonial act, a ritual such as a ceremony.

parts.note: Victorian values are prudish, so prim
or is gold in heraldry
to dial is to ring on the phone

explanation.surface: An authentic nineteenth-century gold ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like jewellery but is the verb, to phone, giving DIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Primordial means existing from the beginning, first in time, which is original in its root sense.

clue.text: Infinitesimal or tiny amounts, say, principally

definitions.text: Infinitesimal or tiny amounts, say, principally

indicators.note: principally means chiefly, at the head, so the first letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: A description of minute quantities, mainly.
explanation.definitionFit: Iotas are very small amounts, from the smallest letter of the Greek alphabet.

indicators.note: reported means spoken of, so the word is as heard aloud

parts.note: a river's course is its flow

explanation.surface: News of a route for an iceberg.
explanation.definitionFit: A floe is a sheet of floating ice, a mass of ice drifting on the sea.

indicators.note: loaded can mean drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Robbers armed with a gun attack someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' reads as a verb about a street robbery; here it is the noun, a gullible person.
explanation.definitionFit: A mug is British slang for a fool or someone easily duped, the same as a simpleton.

clue.text: At the top, it's cold initially

definitions.text: At the top, it's cold initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: Up in the roof space it starts out chilly.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic is the room right under the roof, the highest part of a house, often chilly.

indicators.note: whipped means beaten or quickly stirred, so the letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A cad snatches away some lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' is part of the definition: lingerie is one kind of underclothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Underclothes are garments worn beneath outer clothing, and lingerie is a women's example.
